facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Marriage Gifts 100% Exempt: Gifts received on the occasion of the individual's marriage carry zero tax liability.
facts.text: Wedding gifts received by an individual on the occasion of their marriage are completely tax-free without any upper monetary limit.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: All gifts received on the occasion of marriage are 100% tax-exempt under Section 56(2)(x) with no monetary limit;
facts.text: All wedding gifts received during marriage are exempt under Section 56(2)(x) regardless of value or asset class.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: Under Section 271DA, the Joint Commissioner of Income Tax shall levy a 100% monetary penalty on the recipient equal to the cash amount received!
facts.text: Violating Section 269ST by accepting cash gifts of 2 lakh rupees or higher triggers a mandatory 100 percent penalty under Section 271DA on the recipient.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The income tax officer might check for the genuineness of the transaction and if they feel that there is no satisfactory proof or explanation, they might levy 60% tax along with interest and penalty.
facts.text: If high-value wedding gifts lack satisfactory documentation or proof of genuineness during tax scrutiny, assessing officers can levy a 60 percent tax along with interest and penalty.

intro.prompt: 9:16 vertical, 1080x1920, about 8 seconds, photorealistic and cinematic, bright vivid colour. Setting: close view of a decorated wedding stage table in an Indian banquet hall at night, a heap of colourful shagun envelopes beside marigold garlands, warm yellow fairy lights, shallow depth of field. The background is real and in motion behind him (as fits the place: waves, mist, leaves, flags, lamps flickering, people walking, traffic, light shifting); never a still, flat or heavily blurred backdrop. Framing: medium shot from the waist up, his whole head and both shoulders inside the frame with clear space above his hair and on both sides, and he stays framed like this to the end; do not crop the top of his head. Lighting: warm key light on the face, a soft rim light on the hair, matched to the scene; flattering, no harsh shadows, no dull or flat grey look. SG [locked] standing relaxed and upright, shoulders open, wearing a charcoal grey blazer over a light blue shirt. Speaks from the first frame, mouth matched to the words, steady eye contact with the lens. Face and delivery: a confident, charismatic documentary presenter. Calm, natural face with a pleasant, warm smile, relaxed eyebrows, eyes soft and focused on the viewer. On "shagun mila, tax lagega" the eyes narrow a little with intrigue and the head tilts slightly, as if sharing a secret. On "Ab suniye, ye chaunkane wali baat hai!" a warm, confident smile and one small nod. Natural blinking, subtle head movement. No exaggerated expressions: no wide eyes, no raised eyebrows, no open-mouth surprise, no big grin, no frown; never sad, gloomy, worried or tired. Voice: warm, clear, measured, with quiet intensity; a short pause before "shagun mila, tax lagega". Hands: one slow, small gesture toward the scene behind him on the first line, then hands rest; no fast or large arm movements. Camera: eye level, a very slight slow push-in, slight handheld feel. Empty hands, no prop. @SGLearning watermark in the top right corner, white, bold, 80% opacity. No captions, no subtitles, no other on-screen text. No hologram, no floating screen, no graph, no chart, no laptop, tablet, monitor, TV or glowing blue panel anywhere in the frame. Export at 1080x1920.
